skill.name: readme
skill.description: Generate or update a comprehensive README.md after reviewing project structure, dependencies, setup steps, architecture, tests, deployment, and troubleshooting details.
skill.summary: Creates thorough README.md files for software projects.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, inline code, placeholder configuration, and user-visible README examples. No prompt injection, hidden command execution, unauthorized network access, or credential exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md. Generated READMEs should still use placeholders for all secrets and private deployment details.

content.value_statement: Incomplete READMEs slow onboarding and hide setup details. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create clear setup, architecture, testing, and deployment documentation.
actual_capabilities: Reviews project structure and common configuration files to infer frameworks, dependencies, scripts, and deployment targets.
Creates README sections for overview, tech stack, prerequisites, setup, architecture, scripts, testing, deployment, and troubleshooting.
Tailors examples for Rails, JavaScript tooling, Docker, Heroku, Fly.io, Render, and Kamal patterns.
Adds environment variable tables and credential setup guidance using placeholders.
Writes a complete README.md file in the project root.
limitations: May produce more detail than small projects need unless the user requests a concise README.
Needs repository access to infer accurate commands, dependencies, and architecture.
Deployment guidance may require user confirmation when platform configuration is missing.
Should not copy real secret values, private keys, or production credentials into documentation.

best_practices: Review generated commands before publishing the README.
Provide business context and target deployment platform when the repository does not make them clear.
Use placeholders for secret values, private URLs, and production credentials.
anti_patterns: Publishing generated documentation that includes real credentials or private keys.
Accepting deployment instructions without checking them against the actual hosting platform.
Using the full template for a small project that needs a short README.

faq.question: Does this skill write the README file directly?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed to generate a complete README.md in the project root.

faq.question: Can it update an existing README?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review the current README and revise sections that no longer match the repository.

faq.question: Which project types does it fit best?
faq.answer: It works best for software repositories with clear setup, scripts, tests, architecture, or deployment needs.

faq.question: Does it need access to the repository?
faq.answer: Repository access is important because the skill infers commands, dependencies, structure, and deployment details from project files.

faq.question: Will it include secret values?
faq.answer: It should use placeholders only. Users should verify that no real credentials are included before publishing.

faq.question: Can it create deployment documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can document deployment flows when the repository contains platform files or the user provides the target platform.
